origin.description: Write an object to the system clipboard.
origin.usage: write_clip(content, object_type = c("auto", "character", "table"), breaks = NULL, eos = NULL, return_new = FALSE, allow_non_interactive = Sys.getenv("CLIPR_ALLOW", interactive()), ...)

arguments.name: content
arguments.text: Object to place on the clipboard.

arguments.name: object_type
arguments.text: auto treats a data frame or matrix as a table and anything else as text. character and table force that choice.

arguments.name: breaks
arguments.text: Separator between elements or table rows. NULL uses the system line break.

arguments.name: eos
arguments.text: Optional terminator written after the text, followed by a nul. NULL writes no terminator.

arguments.name: return_new
arguments.text: If true, return the rendered text. If false, return the original object.

arguments.name: allow_non_interactive
arguments.text: A non-interactive session is refused unless this is TRUE or CLIPR_ALLOW is TRUE.
Further arguments to write.table when the object is a table. The default separator is a tab.

origin.details: Tables are formatted with write.table. Other objects are coerced to text and joined with breaks. On X11, xclip is preferred, then xsel, then wl-copy. Those programs can keep running until the next paste.
origin.value: The original object, invisibly, or the rendered text when return_new is true.
origin.example:
text <- "Write to clipboard"
print(write_clip(text, return_new = TRUE))
multiline <- c("Write", "to", "clipboard")
print(write_clip(multiline, return_new = TRUE))
print(write_clip(multiline, breaks = ",", return_new = TRUE))
tbl <- data.frame(a = c(1, 2, 3), b = c(4, 5, 6))
print(write_clip(tbl, return_new = TRUE))

translation.description: Write an object to the system clipboard.
translation.usage: write_clip(content, object_type="auto", breaks=None, eos=None, return_new=False, allow_non_interactive=None, **options)

arguments.name: content
arguments.text: String, list of strings, dict of columns, Frame, Matrix, or a rectangular list of rows.

arguments.name: object_type
arguments.text: auto treats a dict, Frame, Matrix, or rectangular list as a table. character and table force that choice.

arguments.name: breaks
arguments.text: Separator between elements or table rows. None uses a newline, or a carriage return and newline on Windows.

arguments.name: eos
arguments.text: Optional terminator written after the text, followed by a nul. None writes no terminator.

arguments.name: return_new
arguments.text: If true, return the rendered text. If false, return the original object.

arguments.name: allow_non_interactive
arguments.text: A non-interactive session is refused unless this is True or CLIPR_ALLOW is the string TRUE.

arguments.name: options
arguments.text: write.table options such as sep, na, row.names, and col.names. The default separator is a tab.

translation.details: A dict of equal-length columns is a data frame. A list of rows is a matrix. Tables follow write.table, including the extra leading separator when both row names and column names are written. Numbers follow R's as.character. On Linux the writer calls xclip, then xsel, then wl-copy.
translation.value: The original object, or the rendered text when return_new is true.
translation.example:
from clipr import write_clip
text = "Write to clipboard"
print(write_clip(text, return_new=True))
multiline = ["Write", "to", "clipboard"]
print(write_clip(multiline, return_new=True))
print(write_clip(multiline, breaks=",", return_new=True))
tbl = {"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]}
print(write_clip(tbl, return_new=True))
